claims.statement: The web app boots from apps/web/src/main.tsx, where it creates a TanStack router and React Query client, then renders the app under QueryClientProvider, a dark ThemeProvider, and the shared FontProvider.

The web root route in apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx is the global UI shell: it wraps the app in TooltipProvider and ThemeProvider, mounts the checkout incentive provider/panel and toaster, and only shows React Query and router devtools when VITE_NODE_ENV is development.

apps/web/src/routes/dashboard.tsx is the main conversational workspace hotspot: it fetches the greeting on mount, starts agent turns through runAgentTurnStream, sends follow-up interactions through sendInteractionStream, and coordinates recommendation, comparison, checkout, reasoning, accessory, and retail modal state in one route component.

The resume page consumes a token from the URL, calls the resume API with React Query, removes the token from browser history, invalidates session queries, and navigates to /dashboard with the restored session id; when the token is missing or invalid it renders the expired-token recovery UI instead.

apps/web/src/api/decision-memory.ts is the frontend hotspot for session and agent traffic: it adds Authorization when present, guarantees an X-Anonymous-ID header by generating and persisting one in localStorage when missing, and owns session CRUD, greeting fetch, autosave, branch/restore, chat, streaming chat, and resume helpers plus zod validation of agent envelopes.

The mobile app is currently a shell rather than a major product hotspot: apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx defines the Expo Router stack and native providers, while the current home tab at apps/mobile/app/(drawer)/(tabs)/index.tsx is still placeholder content.

services/main-backend/cmd/retail/main.go is the backend process entrypoint and supports three execution modes: normal server startup through bootstrap.Run, database migrations through -migrate, and metadata seeding through -seed.

services/main-backend/internal/bootstrap/bootstrap.go is the highest-signal backend wiring file because it loads config, connects Postgres, Redis, and the job client, constructs the domain services and handlers, and registers route groups for identity, users, checkout, orders, files, products, accessories, stores, sessions, resume-session, promotions, and admin.
The decision-memory backend handlers use optional bearer auth plus X-Anonymous-ID ownership to scope session access, and they require some identity to create or list sessions.

The backend chat handler persists the new user message, reloads the session history, forwards only user/assistant messages plus extracted comparison-eligible product ids to the AI runtime, validates the returned envelope, and stores the assistant message with the full envelope JSON in ReasoningGraph.

The backend streaming chat path proxies AI runtime SSE events, reconstructs the final assistant message and decision/envelope from streamed events, and persists the assistant response when the stream finishes successfully.

The decision-memory interaction handler is the main dynamic-UI interaction hotspot: it accepts only schema_version 1.0 question.answer submit events, deduplicates work by interaction_id with a leased persisted interaction record, validates that the request matches the currently stored question envelope, and can replay a previously stored response envelope instead of calling the AI runtime again.

The resume-session service enforces single-use token lifecycle rules: generating a new resume token revokes prior unconsumed tokens for the same session, resumption rejects invalid, revoked, consumed, or expired tokens, and successful resume marks the token consumed before returning the session.

The resume-session service treats issuance/consumption context hashes as audit signals rather than hard blockers for cross-device resume, and its inactivity notification flow requires an authenticated session with a verified notification identity before generating a token, sending through the provider, and persisting a notification log.

The AI runtime entrypoint in services/ai-runtime/src/main.py mounts the chat router under /api/v1, adds request-latency logging middleware that also sets X-Process-Time, exposes /health, and converts uncaught exceptions into a structured internal_error JSON response.

services/ai-runtime/src/api/chat.py is the runtime’s main request hotspot: it defines greeting and chat request models, builds an OpenAI provider and backend ToolProxy from settings, serves direct chat responses and SSE chat streaming, and falls back to a canned localized greeting if model-generated greeting creation fails.

The AI runtime workflow in services/ai-runtime/src/graph/workflow.py first loads catalog data and offer comparisons through the backend tool proxy, then invokes the LLM with a strict AgentDraft JSON schema, hydrates the final AgentResponse against backend data, and retries self-correction up to two times when structured output validation fails.

The most important shared contract package for dynamic UI is packages/protocols/src/index.ts, which defines the allowed dynamic component and action types, the InteractionRequest payload shape, and applyUIOperations(), which sorts operations deterministically by sequence and id before replacing surface or nested components.

packages/api-types is the shared TypeScript API payload surface for client code: src/index.ts re-exports identity, decision-memory, and promotions modules; identity.ts defines Zod-backed auth request and token response schemas; and promotions.ts defines checkout incentive trigger and promotion status payloads.

The highest-signal tests to open before changing active flows are the web decision-memory and resume tests, backend decision-memory chat and resume-session tests, AI runtime graph and self-correction tests, and backend OpenAPI contract tests, because they cover anonymous/session headers, SSE parsing, ownership, token lifecycle, workflow hydration, bounded retries, and documented API surface expectations.

The highest-signal specs to open before changing current product flows are specs/005-decision-memory/spec.md, specs/007-resume-shopping-session/spec.md, and specs/008-llm-integration/spec.md, because they define the repository’s intended behavior for autosave/branching, secure resume-link handling, and AI runtime streaming plus structured-output requirements.
